I5.quote: The reported hydrogen uptake of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) has been the subject of much controversy.

notes: Original volumetric (Sieverts) H2 uptake measurements on six CNT samples (as-prepared and purified SWCNTs; as-prepared, air-oxidized, CO2-oxidized and KOH-activated MWCNTs) at about 12 MPa and 19.0-23.0 C (Table 1), with a specific surface area given for every sample in Table 1. No 77 K data. The article's first sentence of body text (Introduction) is also English: 'Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) possess a unique hollow tubular structure, large surface area, and desirable chemical and thermal stability.' Not a review: it reports new measurements. record.json is_retracted is false and the PDF carries no retraction notice. duplicate_data does not apply: the paper does not state that its H2 uptake values were published before; it says the authors' earlier (1999) capacities were overestimated, and refers to ref. [18] only for the treatment procedure and characterization of the MWCNT samples. The paper also reports 0.7-0.9 wt.% for three samples on a second apparatus (Kiyobayashi et al., ref. [19]) without per-sample values; this is not needed for eligibility.
